  • Human Editorial Exemptions: Content does not require an AI label if it has undergone substantive human review and editing where a named person takes responsibility. Small assistive edits like spellcheck or color correction are not considered AI generation under these rules.
  • Defining Substantive Editing: The line between 'edited' and 'generated' depends on manual intervention; automated generation always requires disclosure while fine-tuning human-written text does not. A simple 'skim' before publishing does not qualify as a valid human editorial review.
  • Standardized UI Requirements: Ambiguous 'sparkle' icons are insufficient for compliance; the EU mandates specific AI icons paired with plain-language labels. These indicators must be accessible, clearly visible, and persist even when content is downloaded or shared.
  • Global Regulatory Convergence: The EU's move reflects a global trend, with similar AI labeling laws already active or pending in California, China, India, and South Korea. This shift suggests that AI transparency is becoming a standard international compliance requirement.
